issues.body: `LOADER_ALIAS` requires the loader token immediately after `=`, while `LOADER_CALL` requires it immediately before `(`. Consequently a paper can use `#let grab = (json)`, then `#let d = grab("/src/data/paper-" + "timing.generated.json")`, and render `d.records...value`; neither regex matches the grouped `json` token. This reaches the raw generated timing without either provenance-rendering accessor, contradicting the gate's fail-closed claim. The load-bearing test only exercises the ungrouped `#let grab = json` form, so it does not detect this bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Reject loader identifiers used as values through harmless grouping (at minimum parenthesized aliases), and add the exact grouped-alias construction to the negative bypass fixtures so the real `auditTimingSources` path must report it. More generally, prefer a token/parser-aware check of loader references in Typst code positions over enumerating only direct-call and one alias syntax.
issues.title: Parenthesized loader aliases bypass the source gate

verdict.summary: Round 7 regresses from round 6's clean approval: the publication-boundary gate still has a simple loader-alias bypass. `LOADER_ALIAS` recognizes only a bare loader immediately after `=`, so valid Typst grouping can hide the loader name while retaining the callable value. The current negative test covers `#let grab = json` but not this grouped form, making the claimed fail-closed rendering boundary incomplete.
